intuition: In a word square, row r and column r must spell the same word. When choosing the next row, its first letters are already fixed by the earlier rows. Use a prefix index to find only words that start with those letters, then try each possible continuation.

Index each word under all its prefixes. At depth k, read character k from each existing row and join those letters into the required prefix. The map immediately supplies only words that could fit. This reference uses a prefix-to-word-list dictionary rather than traversing a trie.

Backtracking then appends each compatible candidate and undoes it afterward. Words may be reused because the problem does not limit occurrences. Each appended row preserves all established row-column crossings, so a path containing the required number of rows is a complete valid square without a separate full symmetry scan.

Only proper prefixes are queried: when k reaches the word length, the base case saves the completed square before another lookup. The reference therefore indexes prefix lengths zero through L-1 and omits the unused full-length entry. This saves one stored reference per word while preserving every candidate needed by the search.

steps: All fixture words have length four. Index prefixes of area, lead, wall, lady, and ball, including the empty prefix for the first row.
Consider the branch beginning with ball. At depth 1, column 1 of ball gives prefix "a", selecting area.
With rows ball and area, depth 2 reads their column-2 letters l and e. Prefix "le" selects lead.
At depth 3, the crossing letters are l, a, and d. Prefix "lad" selects lady, completing [ball,area,lead,lady].
The branch starting wall requires the same later prefixes and completes [wall,area,lead,lady]. Other starting rows cannot finish, leaving two squares.

codeNotes.note: One word is listed under each usable prefix, so later searches retrieve candidates directly instead of repeatedly scanning the full dictionary.
The kth character of each existing row is already fixed in column k. Reading those crossings derives the only possible next-row prefix.
A missing prefix has no compatible candidate and ends the branch immediately. Existing words remain reusable, so no used-word set is applied.

keyDecision: At row k, the required prefix is square[0][k], square[1][k], through square[k - 1][k].

concept.question: How can the next row be forced by the columns already chosen?
intuition: Trying arbitrary word sequences ignores the square condition until too late. Once earlier rows exist, their letters in the next column already determine the beginning of the next row.
Index words by prefixes. At row depth d, read column d of every chosen row to form the required prefix. Branch only among words with that prefix, and undo the choice after exploring it.
concept.observation: The next row must begin with the letters already present in its matching column.
approach: Index each word under all its prefixes.
Build the next required prefix from the chosen rows’ column letters.
Explore matching next words until a complete square is formed.
concept.correctness: When a new row is chosen, its required prefix checks every symmetric pair against earlier rows. Later rows will check the remaining pairs. A completed square therefore satisfies every row-column equality. Conversely, every valid square’s next word has exactly the required prefix, so the branching search cannot exclude it.

complexity.time: O(W * L^2 + L * W^L) worst case
complexity.space: O(W * L^2 + L) auxiliary, excluding output
complexity.explanation: Prefix indexing reduces the candidates at each depth, but the search can still branch exponentially in word length. Index storage includes copied prefixes; the working square has only one word per row, in addition to returned squares.

pitfalls: The next row must begin with the letters already present in its matching column.
Do not require the next word to share a prefix with the preceding word.

scenes.narration: For area,lead,wall,lady,ball, start with ball. The next row must start with a because column one of ball is a.
scenes.decision: The first row has no earlier column constraints.

scenes.title: Column constraints grow
scenes.narration: Choose area. The third row must start with le: ball contributes l and area contributes e. Choose lead.
scenes.decision: Every added row must match all previously fixed symmetric positions.

scenes.title: Finish a valid square
scenes.narration: The last required prefix is lad, selecting lady. This yields ball/area/lead/lady. Starting with wall yields the other valid square wall/area/lead/lady.
scenes.decision: Every row equals its corresponding column.
